title: Lipoarabinomannan as a named amphiphile
dek: LAM/ManLAM on Wikipedia is an envelope glycolipid. Urine LF-LAM as a diagnostic is tb-lf-lam.
story: Lipoarabinomannan on Wikipedia is a phosphatidylinositol-anchored glycolipid in the mycobacterial envelope, mannose-capped (ManLAM) in pathogenic species in the usual telling, and a modulator of innate recognition.
Urine lateral-flow LAM is a diagnostic that detects fragments of this molecule in advanced HIV. That assay has a clinic plate. This card is the molecule the strip is trying to see.
Do not confuse envelope LAM with the LF-LAM brand names, or with lipopolysaccharide from Gram-negatives.
deep: PIM/LM/LAM biosynthetic steps are research-layer; INH they are not.
Immune modulation stories (TLR, mannose receptor) are pointers, not DST.
LF-LAM sensitivity is a function of burden and CD4, on tb-lf-lam.
Sputum LAM assays are a different product class if they appear on Wikipedia later.

visual.caption: Envelope molecule in the middle; urine strip as a diagnostic side-door that only fires in the right host context.
